newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU states reject Commission's fur ban compromise.
newsitem.headline: EU states reject Commission's fur ban compromise.

text.p: EU member states have rejected a European Commission plan for a compromise with Canada, Russia and the United States on rules for animal traps, a Commission source said on Tuesday.

The Commission presented its plan last month, rejecting calls made days earlier by EU environment ministers for a ban on fur imports from Canada, Russia and the United States to try to force new talks on standards for leg-hold traps.

The source said nine of the EU's 15 countries had formally reacted to the Commission proposal, and seven had rejected it, which meant ministers would now have to deal with the issue in a formal meeting.
"Member states have reacted in accordance to their positions at their December meeting," the source said.

Ministers said the trap-standards deal brokered between the EU, Canada and Russia during 1996 did not go far enough in that it would ban only steel-jawed traps while leaving less clear the fate of padded traps, whose main difference compared with steel-jawed devices is that their jaws carry rubber strips.
At issue are standards for traps intended to kill or catch 18 species of wild animals, including muskrats, beavers, sable, lynx and wolves.

The Commission, largely at the urging of European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, ignored environment ministers' instructions to prepare the import ban against all three countries, preferring to recommend approval of the draft deal worked out with Russia and Canada while continuing work on a threatened ban against U.S. imports.
Member states' rejection of the proposal means that multilateral talks on standards remain on ice while the European Union sorts out its internal wranglings.

The EU has repeatedly delayed implementation of its planned ban on fur from countries without suitable leg-hold trap standards, prompting anger among animal rights activists and the European Parliament.
